passages.note: Prime sponsorship of a deepfake-impersonation cause of action, a dimension the platform-duty ladder does not order.

passages.provision_quote: A provider of an interactive computer service may not be subject to an action for DIGITAL IMPERSONATION for PUBLISHING INFORMATION that is provided by another information content provider.
passages.note: The operative section creates a private civil action against the publisher of a digital impersonation and expressly exempts interactive computer services, so it imposes no platform duty at all.
House Final Reading passed with no member voting no, so the vote separates nobody even apart from relevance.

rows.reasoning: The only evidence is HB2394 (2024), which Kolodin prime-sponsored and voted for: it gives an impersonated person a court action against whoever published a deepfake of them, and expressly shields interactive computer services from that action. It therefore sets no platform obligation, so it cannot reach "legally require platforms to remove false information" or "require platforms to label false content, rather than remove it", and it is not a limit on state content moderation, so it cannot reach "protect free speech online and prevent government censorship" or "ban any government involvement in content moderation decisions" either. No passage addresses the dimension the rungs separate.
